body:
<!-- plain-summary -->
To check Wyrd's behavior from the outside, an external tool needs a network interface it can send storage operations to (write, read, list, rename, delete) while recording exactly when each one started and finished. This step builds that observable networked client, so the consistency checker has real operations and a real timeline to test against.

**Slice 2 of #329.** The literal external checker needs a networked client interface to drive — there is none today (the gateway is in-process, `crates/server/src/lib.rs:8` "HTTP/S3 wire surface is a later milestone"; only the fragment-level gRPC ChunkStore is networked).

**Scope:**
- Drive **overwriting PUT / GET / list / rename / delete** against the S3 HTTP wire surface (**#364**) — the object path is the mutable register; overwrite = a new inode version.
- Record **client-observed real-time order** (per-op start/end timestamps) so the checker has a real-time order to validate against.
- Fallback if #364 slips: a thin client-facing gRPC/HTTP shim exposing the same ops.

**Depends on:** #364 (S3 HTTP wire surface). **Refs:** #329, ADR-0041, ADR-0015 (guarantee 2).

milestone.description: Step 2. Swap embedded redb for distributed TiKV behind the unchanged MetadataStore trait; multi-key atomic directory ops hold under the distributed store. Completes the single-zone data plane — a soft stopping point, not the release: the ★ Step-2 release point is M8 (proposal 0013 implementation arc, supersedes 0002). Plan: proposal 0015 (supersedes 0007; acceptance PR #417); tracker #201; first-deployment gate #367.
